name: Fastmail Bug Bounty
rights: Original summary CC BY 4.0; linked sources and trademarks retain their own rights.

program_type.summary: The official policy explicitly offers monetary bounties for eligible reports.

rewards.summary: Qualifying reports advertise USD 100–5,000, determined by severity and affected users at Fastmail’s discretion. Payments are processed monthly through PayPal; recipients bear taxes and fees. These are guidelines, not individual awards.

eligibility.summary: First reports must demonstrate a qualifying threat to private user data or infrastructure. Use controlled test accounts; interacting with another account requires its owner’s consent. Responsible disclosure and reasonable remediation time are required.

restrictions.summary: Protect data integrity, privacy and service availability. Disruption and social engineering are prohibited. Intended email behavior, unlikely-interaction findings, third-party services, username enumeration, obsolete clients and low-impact metadata are excluded.

submission_status.summary: The policy expressly invites immediate email reports and commits to investigating all legitimate submissions. This is published intake evidence, not a delivery test.

limitations: The reward sentence explicitly uses US$ for its minimum; the adjoining dollar maximum belongs to that same schedule.
No revision date, change log, age or residency criterion was established. No submission was made. Live terms prevail; no testing authorization is granted.

scope_context.included_summary: Fastmail-operated code and infrastructure; qualifying issues must threaten private data or infrastructure access.
scope_context.excluded_summary: Third-party browser-extension weaknesses and XSS confined to isolated user-content hosting are excluded.

in_scope.name: Fastmail-operated code and infrastructure
in_scope.note: Qualifying impact must involve private user data or Fastmail infrastructure.

in_scope.name: app.fastmail.com
in_scope.note: Named as an example within the XSS-eligible *.fastmail.com domain.

out_of_scope.name: user.fm
out_of_scope.note: XSS on this isolated user-content host is explicitly excluded; this is not a claim that every vulnerability type is excluded.

out_of_scope.name: fastmailusercontent.com
out_of_scope.note: XSS on this isolated user-content host is explicitly excluded; this is not a claim that every vulnerability type is excluded.

out_of_scope.name: www.fastmailfbl.com
out_of_scope.note: Associated site not operated by Fastmail; not bounty eligible.

limitations: The policy defines impact and ownership requirements, not a complete list of Fastmail-operated hosts.
The two user-content domain exclusions are specific to XSS.
